status: PASS, with one plan correction it produced

cost.note: 5 small files, VM to PC and back. Nothing of value was transferred.

what_it_validates: The LAST stage of the pipeline - the one the entire run exists to deliver - and the only probe that puts bytes on the operator's machine. Proving it on a dummy payload is worth more than discovering a failure after 30 hours of finished work depends on it.

byte_identity.method: SHA-256 of every file computed on the VM, then again on the PC after scp -r
byte_identity.verdict: PASS - scp -r is byte-exact, as expected for a binary transfer

typography_survival.why_this_is_the_test: The plan forbids PowerShell pipelines by name because 'Get-Content -Raw | Set-Content -Encoding utf8' and 'python -c "..."' both corrupt non-ASCII. This payload deliberately ships exactly the typography those two approaches destroy.

RESULTS.line_endings: LF authored, LF delivered. No CRLF translation.
RESULTS.bom: absent at source and absent at destination

THE_FINDING_THIS_PROBE_PRODUCED.what_happened: A deliberately planted .mp3 file in the source tree ARRIVED on the PC. My original design treated that as a failure, expecting the transfer to filter media.
THE_FINDING_THIS_PROBE_PRODUCED.why_that_expectation_was_wrong: scp -r copies whatever it is given. The transfer is a DUMB BINARY PIPE and has no filter, and it should not have one. My poison test was testing a control that does not exist at that layer.
THE_FINDING_THIS_PROBE_PRODUCED.where_constraint_1_actually_lives: In vault ASSEMBLY - vault/ receives .md files only - and in gate V6.

THE_PLAN_CORRECTION_THIS_FORCES.change: V6 (zero media extensions under vault/) MUST run on the VM SOURCE TREE BEFORE THE COPY, not on the destination.
THE_PLAN_CORRECTION_THIS_FORCES.why: Once a media file lands on the operator's PC, Constraint 1 has already been violated. A post-copy gate reports a violation that has already happened. The gate has to run upstream of the only irreversible step in the whole pipeline.
THE_PLAN_CORRECTION_THIS_FORCES.sequencing: assemble vault/ -> V6 on VM -> V7 reduction diff -> V12 identity binding -> ONLY THEN scp -> V11 SHA256 compare on the PC

the_only_sanctioned_transfer: scp -r, from the PC pulling from the VM, with the operator's key. No shell pipeline, no text-mode transfer, no re-encoding at any hop. The key lives on the PC, so the copy is always PC-initiated; running scp from the VM fails on host resolution and is not a supported direction.
note_on_my_own_first_attempt: The first version of this probe ran scp FROM the VM, which failed because the SSH private key is on the PC. That is an architecture error, not a transfer error: egress is always PC-initiated. Recorded because the failure mode (rc=255, 'Could not resolve hostname c') looks like a network fault and is not.
residual_risk: The vault is ~4-5 million words across 339 notes. Total transfer size is markdown only, so single-digit megabytes. At the measured scp throughput this is seconds, not minutes. The 7-phase teardown and the deliberate --confirm <sha256> gate on final destroy are unaffected.
